questions.question: Who was Tutankhamun?
questions.expected_answer: Tutankhamun was a pharaoh who lived about three thousand three hundred years ago. He became king at about nine, ruled for about ten years with the help of officials, and died at about eighteen or nineteen. During his rule, the old gods were restored after Akhenaten's changes. Later pharaohs removed his name from king lists, so he was almost forgotten.

questions.question: Explain who found the tomb, when, and why they were searching.
questions.expected_answer: Howard Carter, a British archaeologist, found it, with his team, and Lord Carnarvon paid for the digging. Many experts thought all the tombs in the Valley of the Kings had been found, but Carter believed Tutankhamun's tomb was still hidden because small objects with his name had been found there. After years of searching, his workers found the first step on 4 November 1922.

questions.question: Describe how the tomb was opened.
questions.expected_answer: Workers uncovered sixteen steps to a sealed doorway. On 26 November 1922, Carter made a hole in a second doorway and by candlelight saw gold everywhere, wonderful things. The antechamber was full of objects. In 1923 they entered the burial chamber with its shrines, a stone coffin and three coffins, the innermost of solid gold, and in 1925 reached the mummy. Recording everything took about ten years.
